2 GENERAL INFORMATION
2.1 Introduction
               This document details the design and implementation of a SEMI Equipment Communications
               Standard (SECS) interface that conforms to the Generic Model for communications and
               control of SEMI equipment (GEM).
               The SEMI Equipment Communications Standard (SECS) defines an interface suitable for the
               exchange of messages between computers in a semiconductor factory.
               This implementation is built upon three layers of standards:
                       SEMI E37
                       SEMI E5
                       SEMI E30
               SEMI E37 (HSMS) defines a communication interface suitable for the exchange of messages
               between computers in a semiconductor factory using a TCP/IP environment. TCP/IP stream
               support is used to provide reliable two-way simultaneous transmissions of streams of
               contiguous bytes. This implementation supports TCP/IP running on Ethernet.
               SEMI E5 (SECS-II) defines the details necessary for the interpretation of messages exchanged
               between a Host and equipment. It is the intent of this standard to define sufficient detail to
               enable Host software to be built with only minimal knowledge of the opposite side of the
               communications link.
               SEMI E30 (GEM) defines the behaviour of semiconductor equipment as viewed through the
               communications link. It defines which SECS-II messages should be used, in what situations
               and the resultant activity.

2.2 Supported Software Revisions
               This GEM/SECS II Interface described in this manual requires the equipment software to be at
               Release 9.9.5 or higher with the Cimetrix-based SECS Module installed.

4 Communications
4.1 Objective
               Orderly transitions of communication link between normal communications and non-
               communicating states.

4.2 Communications State Model
               The Communications State Model defines the behaviour of the equipment in relation to the
               existence or absence of a communications link with the Host.
               The State Diagram shown in Figure 1 below details the Communications Finite State Model
               that the SPTS fxP Equipment maintains, and Table 2 shows the corresponding
               Communications Transition Table. Section 4.2.3 describes each state of the model.

     4.2.3     Communications State Definitions
                       The SPTS fxP equipment CTC User Interface will display the current Communication State:

                        DISABLED
                        ENABLED/NOT COMMUNICATING
                        ENABLED/COMMUNICATING


                       The possible communication states are as follows:
     4.2.3.1    DISABLED
                               The SECS link with the Host is non-existent. The SPTS fxP equipment will not send
                               any messages to the Host and will not respond to any messages from the Host.
     4.2.3.2    ENABLED
                               The ENABLED state assumes that lower level protocols such as SECS-I or HSMS
                               are fully functional and for the Equipment to be in communication with the Host.
                               When communications are enabled, either by operator selection or system
                               initialisation, the sub-state of NOT COMMUNICATING will be active until the
                                                            11
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


                       formal establishment of communications, and then COMMUNICATING will be
                       active.
4.2.3.3   COMMUNICATING
                       In this state, communications between Host and the SPTS fxP equipment are
                       operating normally. All messages from the Host may be received.
                       The equipment will send a ‘heartbeat’ message (S1F1) periodically to test if the link
                       is still operating. The equipment constant HEARTBEAT defines the period between
                       these messages. If the constant is zero, no heartbeat messages will be sent.
                       If a communications failure occurs, the equipment will return to the NOT
                       COMMUNICATING State.
4.2.3.4   NOT COMMUNICATING
                       In this state, the SECS link to the Host is enabled at the SPTS fxP equipment, and the
                       equipment is attempting to determine if the link is active. The equipment periodically
                       sends S1F13 (Establish Communications Request).
                       If the connection is not successful for any reason, the equipment will periodically
                       attempt to establish communications. The time between attempts is controlled by the
                       equipment constant ESTABLISHCOMMUNICATIONSTIMEOUT.
                       Once the Host has responded with S1F14, the Communication State will change to
                       COMMUNICATING.
                       In the event that the Host and the equipment attempt to establish communications at
                       the same time, the following two ‘AND’ sub-states of the NOT COMMUNICATING
                       State clarify the behaviour of the equipment.

                          EQUIPMENT-INITIATED CONNECT

                          HOST-INITIATED CONNECT
                       If the equipment constant ESTABLISHCOMMUNICATIONSTIMEOUT is set to
                       zero, the equipment will never initiate a Connect Request and will expect the Host to
                       initiate.
4.2.3.5   NOT COMMUNICATING/EQUIPMENT-INITIATED CONNECT
                       On entry to the NOT COMMUNICATING State, the SPTS fxP equipment will
                       immediately attempt to send an S1F13.
                       A transition to WAIT CRA occurs.
4.2.3.6   NOT COMMUNICATING/EQUIPMENT-INITIATED CONNECT/WAIT CRA
                       The SPTS fxP equipment waits for the Host to acknowledge the S1F13 that has been
                       sent.

4.2.3.7   NOT COMMUNICATING/EQUIPMENT-INITIATED CONNECT/WAIT DELAY
                       The connection attempt is unsuccessful; the SPTS fxP equipment will wait for the
                       period of time determined by the equipment constant
                       ESTABLISHCOMMUNICATIONSTIMEOUT before retrying the S1F13.

4.2.3.8   NOT COMMUNICATING/HOST-INITIATED CONNECT
                       On entry to NOT COMMUNICATING State, the SPTS fxP equipment will
                       immediately enter the WAIT CR FROM HOST State and begins to wait for an
                       S1F13 from the Host.
4.2.3.9   NOT COMMUNICATING/HOST-INITIATED CONNECT/WAIT CR FROM HOST
                       The SPTS fxP equipment is waiting for an S1F13 from the Host.
                       If an S1F13 is received, the SPTS fxP equipment will attempt to send an S1F14 with
                       COMMACK=0.


                                                   12
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


4.3 Associated Variables
                 The following Equipment Constants are relevant to the operation of the SPTS fxP equipment
                 Communications State Model.

                  DefaultCommState - default entry state at initialisation

                  EstablishCommunicationsTimeout - delay before retrying S1F13

                  HeartBeat- time between S1F1 messages

5 Control
5.1 Objective
               The orderly cooperation between the Host system and the SPTS fxP equipment operator in
               controlling the equipment.

5.2 State Model
               The CONTROL model provides the Host with three basic levels of control:

                  OFF-LINE
                  LOCAL
                  REMOTE
               For the lowest level, OFF-LINE, no Host control is allowed and very limited information is
               available. The middle level, LOCAL, offers limited control to the Host but full access to
               information. The highest level, REMOTE, gives the Host the fullest extent of control over the
               SPTS fxP equipment.
               The state diagram shown in Control State Diagram


                   POWER UP

                                                                      1           C


                           OFFLINE                                    2           C

                                   EQUIPMENT                              3
                                    OFFLINE


                                          12                          C            ATTEMPT
                                                                              4
                                                                                    ONLINE

                            6         HOST
                                     OFFLINE
                                                                                        5

                                     11        10



                           ONLINE
                                                                  7               C


                                                                  8
                                      LOCAL                                           REMOTE
                                                                  9




                                                    14
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


               Figure 2 below shows the relationship between these and the other sub-states. Table 4 shows
               the corresponding State Transition table.

5.2.3      Control State Definitions
5.2.3.1     OFF-LINE
                           In this state, the SECS link is severely restricted. All SPTS fxP equipment controls
                           are actioned by the operator.
                           The equipment will only send and respond to messages that are required for
                           CONNECT and ON-LINE, S1F13 and S1F17.
                           The equipment will refuse primary messages from the Host by responding with a
                           SxF0.
                           The OFF-LINE State has three sub-states:

                                 EQUIPMENT OFF-LINE
                                 ATTEMPT ON-LINE
                                 HOST OFF-LINE




                                                           16
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


5.2.3.2   OFF-LINE/EQUIPMENT OFF-LINE
                       In this Offline sub-state, only the SPTS fxP equipment can switch to Online (through
                       the operator interface). The OFF-LINE State is maintained until the operator requests
                       ON-LINE. Transition to OFF-LINE/ATTEMPT ON-LINE occurs.
                       If an S1F13 (Connect Request) is received from the Host, the SPTS fxP equipment
                       will respond with S1F14 (Connect Acknowledge).
                       If an S1F17 (On-line Request) is received from the Host, the equipment will respond
                       with S1F18 (On-line Acknowledge) with a non-zero acknowledge code rejecting the
                       request.
5.2.3.3   OFF-LINE/ATTEMPT ON-LINE
                       While this state is active, the SPTS fxP equipment is attempting to go ON-LINE at
                       the request of the operator.
                       The equipment will send an S1F1 (Are you there) to the Host.
                       If an S1F13 (Connect Request) is received from the Host, the equipment will respond
                       with S1F14 (Connect Acknowledge).
                       If an S1F17 (On-line Request) is received from the Host, the equipment will respond
                       with S1F18 (On-line Acknowledge).
                       If an S1F2 (On-line Data) is received from the Host, a transition to ON-LINE occurs.
                       The equipment constant ONLINESUBSTATE defines the sub-state, either LOCAL
                       or REMOTE. The appropriate Control event, ControlStateLOCAL or
                       ControlStateREMOTE is signalled.
5.2.3.4   OFF-LINE/HOST OFF-LINE
                       From this Offline sub-state, only the Host can switch the SPTS fxP equipment
                       Online.
                       If the Host sends an S1F17 (Request On-line), the equipment will respond with
                       S1F18 (On-line Acknowledge) with ONLACK=0 and a transition to ON-LINE will
                       occur. The equipment constant ONLINESUBSTATE defines the sub-state, either
                       LOCAL or REMOTE. The appropriate Control event, ControlStateLOCAL or
                       ControlStateREMOTE is signalled.
                       If the operator selects Off-line, a transition to OFF-LINE/EQUIPMENT OFF-LINE
                       occurs, and an EquipmentOFFLINE event is signalled.
                       If an S1F13 (Connect Request), the equipment will respond with S1F14 (Connect
                       Acknowledge).
5.2.3.5   ON-LINE
                       In this state, the SECS link works with few restrictions.
                       The SPTS fxP equipment may send S1F1 (Are you there) and S1F13 (Connect
                       Request) according to the configuration, see section Establishing Connection.
                       The equipment will not send any SxF0 messages.
                       If an S1F13 (Connect Request) is received from the Host, the equipment will respond
                       with S1F14 (Connect Acknowledge).
                       If an S1F15 (Request Off-line) is received from the Host, the equipment will respond
                       with S1F16 (Off-line Acknowledge) and a transition to OFF-LINE/HOST OFF-LINE
                       will occur.
                       If an S1F17 (Request On-line) is received from the Host, the equipment will respond
                       with an S1F18 (On-line Acknowledge) with ONLACK=2 (Equipment already on-
                       line).
                       The ON-LINE State has two sub-states:

                                                   17
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


                           LOCAL

                           REMOTE

5.2.3.6   ON-LINE/LOCAL
                        In this state, the SECS link is operating normally.
                        The operator has full control of the machine.
                        The Host will not allow the use of the S2F41 (Remote Command).
                        If the operator selects Remote, a transition to ON-LINE/REMOTE occurs and a
                        ControlStateREMOTE event is signalled.
                        If the operator selects Off-line, a transition to OFF-LINE/EQUIPMENT OFF-LINE
                        occurs and an EquipmentOFFLINE event is signalled.
                        If the Host sends S1F15 (Request Off-line), the SPTS fxP equipment will respond
                        with S1F16 (Off-line Acknowledge) with OFLACK=0, a transition to OFF-
                        LINE/HOST OFF-LINE occurs and an EquipmentOFFLINE event is signalled.
5.2.3.7   ON-LINE/REMOTE
                        In this state, the SECS link is operating normally.
                        The SPTS fxP equipment operator and the Host share control of the machine based
                        upon a set of Remote Control equipment constants. See the section on Remote
                        Control for further details.
                        If the operator selects Local, a transition to ON-LINE/LOCAL occurs and a
                        ControlStateLOCAL event is signalled.
                        If the operator selects Off-line, a transition to OFF-LINE/EQUIPMENT OFF-LINE
                        occurs and an EquipmentOFFLINE event is signalled.
                        If the Host sends S1F15 (Request Off-line), the equipment will respond with S1F16
                        (Off-line Acknowledge) with OFLACK=0, a transition to OFF-LINE/HOST OFF-
                        LINE occurs and an EquipmentOFFLINE event is signalled.



5.3 Associated Variables
               The following variables are relevant to Control State:
               Equipment Constants:

                  DefCtrlOfflineState

                  DefaultCtrlState


               Status Variables:

                  ControlState

                  PreviousControlState


               The current Control State will be displayed on the Status Line of the SPTS fxP equipment
               CTC User Interface.

SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



6 On-line Identification
6.1 Objective
               To provide on-line identification of the SPTS fxP equipment to the Host system.

6.2 Description
               The equipment will respond to an S1F1 ‘Are You There’ Request with an S1F2 message that
               provides the Equipment Model Type and Equipment Software Revision Code.
               The Equipment Model is the fixed string “fxP” for a 200mm tool.
               The Equipment Software Revision Code is a string of the form:
                        wxy{Pz}
               Where w is the major revision number and x and y are the minor revision numbers.
               For Patched releases there will also be a Pz part where z is the patch number
               The revision code relates to the software issue of the equipment’s CTC. This will normally
               change when any part of the system software is changed, including that installed in the
               Process Modules.

6.3 Associated Variables
               The following variables are relevant to On-line identification:
               Status Variables

                MDLN

                SOFTREV




                                                    19
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



7 Event Notification
7.1 Objective
               To provide an orderly and flexible method of notifying the Host when a significant event
               occurs within the SPTS fxP equipment.

7.2 Event Collection
               The equipment provides a comprehensive set of Collection Events.
               The equipment fully supports the S6F11/F12 transaction for event reporting. The appropriate
               Inquire/Grant (S6F5/F6) is supported for those reports that are multi-block.
               The reporting of an event may be disabled on a per event basis by the Host system. See the
               section on Dynamic Event Report Configuration for more detail.
               The Host may request an Event Report at any time by sending an S6F15 message.
               Table 5 details the Collection Events available for the equipment.

7.3 Associated Variables
               The following Equipment Constants are relevant to the operation of the SPTS fxP equipment
               Event Data Collection mechanism.

                WBitS6 - S6 messages with or without W-bit set
               The following Status Variables are relevant to the operation of the equipment Event Data
               Collection mechanism.

                LastCEID - id of the last collection event that occurred

                EventsEnabled - list of events enabled

8 Alarm Management

8.1 Objective
This allows the Equipment to report alarm information to the Host in an orderly manner.

The Equipment supports the S5F1/F2 message that notifies the Host when an alarm is set and cleared.

The Equipment also supports the enabling and disabling of alarms through the S5F3/F4 message.

The Equipment also supports the Host requesting a listing of alarms (S5F5/F6) and a listing of enabled alarms
(S5F7/F8).

There will be a collection event sent whenever an alarm changes state. The ID of the collection event will be
related to the Alarm ID.

Details of Alarm IDs are given in section 8.3.


8.2 Alarm-related Variables
The following alarm-related status variables are supported: -

   AlarmID -This status variable holds the Alarm ID of the most recent alarm.

   AlarmsEnabled -This status variable holds a list of Alarm IDs for all alarms currently enabled.

   AlarmsSet - This status variable holds a list of Alarm IDs for all alarms which are in the alarm state ‘ON’.

   AlarmState - This status variable holds the On/Off state of the most recent alarm.

   ASer - This status variable holds an alarm serial number which is incremented each time there is an alarm
    state change.


The following alarm-related equipment constant is supported :-

   WBitS5 - This equipment constant determines whether the W-bit is set to ‘1’ or ‘0’ when an alarm message
    is sent.




                                                       26
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


8.3 Alarm ID’s
In order to uniquely identify an alarm, Alarm Ids generated by the tool will be dependent on the station that
originates the alarm (e.g. Process Module or CTC) and the station type

Alarm ID =        ( Station Number * 10,000,000 ) +
                  ( Station Type * 100,000 ) +
                  ID offset.

ON CEID =         ( Station Number * 10,000,000 ) +
                  ( Station Type * 100,000 ) +
                  10000 +
                  ID offset.

OFF CEID =        ( Station Number * 10,000,000 ) +
                  ( Station Type * 100,000 ) +
                  1,000,000,000 + 10,000
                  ID offset.

Station Number :-          0 = Transport
                           1 = VCE A
                           2 = Process Module 1
                           3 = Process Module 2
                           4 = Process Module 3
                           5 = Process Module 4
                           6 = Process Module 5
                           7 = Process Module 6
                           8 = VCE B
                           10 = Cool Station


Station Type :-           3 = Forcefill PM
                           4 = Sputter Deposition PM
                          7 = HSE PM
                          9 = Heat PM
                          20 = Level 0/1 Brooks MX Transport
                          21 = Level 0/1 Brooks Coolstation
                          22 = Level 0/1 Brooks MX Cassette
                          23 = Level 0/1 Brooks Inliner
                          24 = Etch PM
                          25 = Deposition RevB PM
                          26 = SoftEtch RevB PM
                          27 = Heat RevB PM
                          34 = Delta APM PM
                          58 = Pro CVE PM

9 Spooling
9.1 Objective
Spooling provides a method for retaining equipment message data that might otherwise be lost due to
communication failure. The motive for producing this functionality is to retain valuable data used to track
material and to improve product quality. The spooling capability fills a gap in the SEMI E5 standard. In the past,
without a spooling capability, the equipment has typically discarded messages that could not be delivered, or
turned messaging off altogether. It is intended that the host initiate the spool unload process immediately
following the reestablishment of communications.

9.2 Description - Enabling Spooling
The equipment provides the host with the ability to enable and disable Spooling for any message (except Stream
1 messages, i.e. S1, F1 and S1, F13) via the S2, F43/F44 transaction. Spooling may be enabled for an entire
Stream, for individual messages within a stream, or for any combination of the two. Streams and Functions not
referenced in this message are not spooled. Spooling can be totally disabled by sending an S2, F43 with a zero
length list for the first item (see S2, F43 definition).



9.3 Spooling State Diagram
                       SPOOLING

                                                                SPOOL
                                                                ACT IVE


                                                                      SPOOL OUT PUT
                                                H*

                                                                 PURGE             T RANSMIT
                                                                 SPOOL               SPOOL

                                    8                                     4       5     6
                                                           3

                         POWER                                            NO SPOOL
                          OFF                                              OUT PUT
                                    7       SPOOL      1
                                           INACT IVE
                                                                           SPOOL
                                                                            NOT
                                                                            FULL

                                                                              2


                                                                           SPOOL
                                           POWER ON                         FULL




9.3.1     Spooling State Definitions
9.3.1.1    POWER OFF
The equipment has lost power for any reason (e.g. power failure, power switch set to off, etc.).
9.3.1.2    POWER ON
The equipment is powered up.

9.3.1.3    SPOOL INACTIVE
This is the normal operating mode. No spooling occurs. The spool area is empty. Primary SECS-II messages are
transmitted normally.




                                                           28
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


9.3.1.4    SPOOL ACTIVE
All primary SECS-II messages ready for sending and for which spooling is enabled (see S2, F43) are directed to
the spool area. All other primary messages, except Stream 1, are discarded. The equipment attempts to send any
generated secondary messages, yet discards them if the attempt to send fails.
Once communications are established, the host must initiate the spool unload sequence to restore full
functionality (see below). Since the equipment will deliver secondary messages, the host may inquire for
information or send commands as needed.
The SPOOL ACTIVE State has two substates, SPOOL LOAD and SPOOL UNLOAD. This means that they
operate independently, though sharing data and some state change stimuli.
9.3.1.5    SPOOL LOAD
The SPOOL LOAD component enters messages into the spool area. It is divided into two substates: SPOOL
NOT FULL and SPOOL FULL. SPOOL NOT FULL is the default entry substate of the parent state SPOOL
LOAD.
9.3.1.6    SPOOL NOT FULL
As primary SECS-II messages are directed to the spool area, the equipment "writes" the SECS-II message to the
end of the spool. Spooling status variables are incremented each time a message is placed in the spool area.
9.3.1.7    SPOOL FULL
In this state, all of the allocated spooling area is filled. The following options are equipment constant controlled.
The first message to be dealt with is that which could not be fit into the spool prior to transition from SPOOL
NOT FULL (see transition table below).
If the "overwrite spool" equipment constant is true, then the equipment deletes as many of the “oldest” records
(e.g. SECS-II messages) contained in the spool area necessary to make space for the new message and then adds
the message. The "total spool count" status variable is incremented whenever a message is submitted to the
spool area. The "actual spool count" status variable is manipulated to keep an accurate count of the number of
messages contained in the spool area. For example, if it is necessary to delete three messages in the spool area to
spool one message, the "actual spool count" SV would have three subtracted and then one added to the total.
If the "overwrite spool" equipment constant is false, then the subsequent primary messages are discarded. When
such a message is discarded, the "total spool count" SV is still incremented.

9.3.1.8    SPOOL UNLOAD
The SPOOL UNLOAD component of SPOOLACTIVE deals with movement of messages out of the spool. It
has an active substate (SPOOL OUTPUT) and a passive substate (NO SPOOL OUTPUT). NO SPOOL
OUTPUT is the default entry substate since the equipment is NOT COMMUNICATING at the time spooling is
initiated. When communications between equipment and host are restored, there is an opportunity for the host to
recover spooled messages. No action is taken until the host initiates the spool output process via the S6, F23
(Request Spooled Data). The host has the option to either receive the spooled messages (see substate
TRANSMIT SPOOL) or discard all messages in the spool (see substate PURGE SPOOL).
9.3.1.9    NO SPOOL OUTPUT
In this state, no messages are removed from the spool.
9.3.1.10   SPOOL OUTPUT
The SPOOL OUTPUT State encompasses the removal of messages from the spool. Its substates are
TRANSMIT SPOOL and PURGE SPOOL.
9.3.1.11   TRANSMIT SPOOL
The host elects to receive all messages contained in the spool area. The equipment is expected to keep track of
the oldest record (i.e. message) within the spool area. When communications are re-established with the host
and transmission of the spool area is started, the oldest record is the first record transmitted then the next oldest
record, etc. There is no prioritization of messages to be sent from the spool.
As each spooled message is successfully transmitted to the host, it is removed from the spool area upon
successful completion of the transaction. The "actual spool count" SV decrements as each message is removed
from the spool. The equipment transmits messages only from the spool area until all spooled messages have
been completely transmitted to the host.

                                                          29
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


Flow control of the spool transmit process is achieved in two ways. First, only one open transaction on the
equipment is allowed during spool unload. Thus, if a message requires a reply, the equipment waits for that
reply before transmitting the next spooled message. Messages that require no reply are transmitted sequentially
as rapidly as the message transfer mechanism will allow.
The second flow control method is to allow the host to limit the maximum number of messages sent from the
spool in response to the S6, F23 request. The "maximum spool transmit" equipment may be set by the host to
achieve this behaviour. If set to five, for example, the equipment will send the first five messages from the spool
and then transition to the NO SPOOL OUTPUT State, awaiting the nextS6, F23 request. There is no event
report generated when the "maximum spool transmit" value is reached. The host is responsible for determining
this situation by one of the following:
counting the messages received
timing out waiting for the next message
inquiring to the equipment for the current value of the "actual spool count" SV
some combination of the above
If the "maximum spool transmit" equipment constant is set to zero, the spool is transmitted completely in
response to S6, F23.
Normal spooling continues during the spool transmit process. If the SPOOL LOAD component transitions to
SPOOL FULL, it does not have any effect on the SPOOL UNLOAD component. Once full, the spool cannot
make the transition back to SPOOL NOT FULL except via the SPOOL INACTIVE State. Space made available
due to the spool unload process is not used in this case.
When a multi-block message is to be transmitted from the spool, any required inquire/grant transaction is
initiated. If the host's response denies permission to send the multi-block message, the equipment discards that
message and continues with the transmit process. This sequence counts as one message in the "maximum spool
transmit" EC count.
SPOOL LOAD and SPOOL UNLOAD may interact when the spool is full and "overwrite spool" EC is True.
During the spool transmit process, spooled messages are removed while new primary messages are written to
the spool. These new messages are overwriting the oldest messages available, unless the process of unloading
has made sufficient spool space available. There is a possibility that unloading and overwriting processes may
compete for control of the same message area. The loss of continuity may be "disorienting" to the host program
receiving the messages. It is expected that the unloading process will be fast relative to the generation of new
messages, so this occurrence will be rare.
Should a communication failure occur during the spool transmit process, spooling continues as before the
transmit process began. However, the spool unload sequence terminates (i.e. transition to NO SPOOL OUTPUT
will occur--see transition table below).
9.3.1.12    PURGE SPOOL
The equipment discards all messages in the spool and, when the spool is empty, "actual spool count" SV
becomes zero.
9.3.2      Spooling State Transition Table

9.3.3   Related Status Variables, Constants and Events


SpoolCountActual – Number of messages actually stored in the spool area. Multi-block inquire/grant messages
are not included in this count.
SpoolCountTotal – Number of messages actually stored in the spool area. Multi-block inquire/grant messages
are not included in this count.
SpoolFullTime – Number of messages actually stored in the spool area. Multi-block inquire/grant messages are
not included in this count.
SpoolStartTime – Number of messages actually stored in the spool area. Multi-block inquire/grant messages are
not included in this count.
SpoolState - The current state of the GEM spooling state machine.




                                                      31
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


9.3.4    Related Equipment Constants
MaxSpoolMessages – Maximum number of messages that can be put into the spool area until it is considered
full as part of the Spooling State Machine. Multi-block inquire/grant messages are not included in this count.
MaxSpoolTransmit – Maximum number of messages that the machine will transmit from the spool area in
response to an S6F23 (transmit spooled messages) request as part of the Spooling State Machine.
OverwriteSpool – Determine whether to overwrite data in the spool area or to discard further messages when the
spool area is full as part of the Spooling State Machine.
SpoolEnabled - Enable or disable the Spooling State Machine.




9.3.5    Related Collection Events
SpoolTransmitFailure – Spool Transmit failure has occurred.
SpoolingActivated – Spooling State Machine has entered the ACTIVE state.
SpoolingDeactivated – Spooling State Machine has entered the DE-ACTIVE state.




                                                       32
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



10 Error Messages
10.1 Objective
               To provide the Host with consistent reports describing the reason for a particular message or
               communication fault as detected by the SPTS fxP equipment.

10.2 Description
               A communication fault occurs when the fxP equipment does not receive an expected message,
               or when either a transaction timer or conversation timer expires.
               A message fault occurs when the fxP equipment receives a message that it cannot process
               because of a defect within the message.
               The fxP equipment supports all Stream 9 messages. It will send the appropriate message
               containing either <MHEAD> or <SHEAD> as required whenever a communication or
               message fault is detected.




                                                    33
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



11 Dynamic Event Report Configuration
11.1 Objective
               To provide a mechanism for the dynamic customization of event reports by the Host system in
               order to inhibit unwanted messages, and provide a sufficient level of detail for the desired
               Collection Events.

11.2 Report Configuration
               The SPTS fxP equipment is supplied with a set of default reports that reside on the hard disk.
               These are linked to the defined collection events. These defaults may be changed by the Host
               using messages S2F33 to S2F40:

                  S2F33 to define the Event Reports

                  S2F35 to link reports to Collection Events

                  S2F37 to enable or disable Event Reports
               The ability to configure the event reporting capability is supported only via the Host interface,
               the operator console does not support this.
               All report definitions, report-to-event links, and the enable/disable status of event reports are
               retained in non-volatile storage.



11.3 Associated Variables
               The following Status Variables are relevant to the operation of the SPTS fxP equipment Event
               Data Collection mechanism.

                LastCEID - id of the last collection event that occurred

                EventsEnabled - list of events enabled




                                                     34
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



12 Variable Data Collection
12.1 Objective
                     To provide the Host system with a mechanism to query for required equipment data variables.

12.2 Variable Data
                     The SPTS fxP equipment will respond to a Host request for variable data using the S6F19/F20
                     messages. The data will be returned in a report that has either been defined by the Host, see
                     section on Dynamic Event Report Configuration, or by using one of the supplied defaults.
                     The distinction between Status Variables and Data Variables is only made when building an
                     S1F4 reply to a Selected Equipment Status Request message (S1F3) that requires “all SVIDs”.
                     For this special case, the reply contains Status Variables only, Data variables and Equipment
                     Constants are excluded.
                     Note that Discrete Data Values (DVVALs) are only guaranteed to be valid when a specific
                     Collection Event occurs.
                     When requesting lists of variable data, certain variables will be reported that are documented
                     here. This is because they are not supported yet.



12.3 GEM Specific Equipment Constants
12.3.1   Objective
                     To provide Host access to selected constant settings relevant to the operation of the SECSII
                     link and the SPTS fxP equipment as a whole.
12.3.2   Capabilities
                     The SPTS fxP equipment will allow the Host to read one or more of the Equipment Constants
                     as defined in this Section using S2F13. The Host will be able to set GEM Equipment
                     Constants using S2F15.

12.4 GEM Specific Status Variables
       A Status Variable provides meaningful data that can be sampled at any time. It is set by the SPTS fxP
       equipment and may be only read by the Host system. Status Variables are updated continuously.
       The Host requests a report of selected variables with an S1F3 message. The Host may also request the
       description of any or all Status variables by sending a Status Variable Namelist Request message
       (S1F11). The SPTS fxP equipment will respond with an S1F12 message providing the name and units
       of the requested variables.

                                 alarm

                                 currently enabled                                                     U4s

                                 Alarm State is ‘ON’                                                   U4s

                                 alarm. A sequential number is assigned
                                 each time an alarm is set.

       12.6 General Equipment Specific Equipment Constants
       12.6.1   Objective
                        To provide Host access to selected constant settings relevant to the operation of the SECSII
                        link and the SPTS fxP equipment as a whole.
       12.6.2   Capabilities
                        The SPTS fxP equipment will allow the Host to get and set the Equipment Constants as
                        defined in this Section using S2F13.
                        There is also a list of general equipment specific equipment constants that are not intended for
                        modification in Appendix C - General Equipment Specific Equipment Constants.
                        The Host may request basic information, such as name, maximum and minimum values, etc.
                        of one or more of the equipment constants as defined in this Section using S2F29.

13 Limits Monitoring
13.1.1   General Description
The Limits Monitoring State Model allows the equipment to monitor certain status and data variable values. It
allows the host to define limit boundaries. The equipment notifies the host using a collection event whenever
configured variables transition across limit boundaries.
The limits monitoring capability provides the host a means of monitoring equipment conditions by a flexible,
efficient and asynchronous method which is consistent across equipment. It eliminates the need for frequent
status variable polling. This capability also allows the host to implement changes in the monitoring range as
needed. This capability has application to both production operation and diagnostic/testing scenarios and it has
applicability to statistical process control.
          Limits monitoring may be configured for each available variable according to this diagram.

               Limit M aximum
                                                         zone

                                                                                        UPPERDB
               Limit                                   dead band
                                                                                        LOWERDB
                                                         zone
               Limit                                                                    UPPERDB =
                                                                                        LOWERDB
                                                         zone
                                                                                        UPPERDB
               Limit                                   dead band

                                                                                        LOWERDB
                                                         zone
               Limit M inimum



Notice that each limit has an upper dead-band and lower dead-band value. The region between the two is called
the dead-band. If the upper and lower dead-band values are equal, then there is no dead-band. The regions above
and below the limit are called zones. A zone transition occurs when the value crosses above the upper dead-band
or below the lower dead-band. The host may define as many limits as desired.
UPPERDB and LOWERDB values are restricted by the following formula:
Limit Maximum ≥ UPPERDB ≥ LOWERDB ≥ Limit Minimum
A limit divides the possible range of variable values into two parts, the upper zone and the lower zone. At any
time, the monitored variable is considered to be in one and only one of these zones. However, as Figure 4.2.2 in
the SEMI E30 manual shows, these two zones have an area of overlap. This is called the dead-band.
The dead-band is a critical element of Limits Monitoring. Its purpose is to prevent a phenomenon known as
chattering -- the repeated changing of zones due to small, rapid fluctuations in variable value while near the
zone boundary. In practice, the value of a variable must reach the opposite boundary of the dead-band before a
zone transition can occur. Thus, if a variable's value reaches the UPPERDB and transitions into the upper zone,
it will not return to the lower zone until it falls back to the LOWERDB. The difference between UPPERDB and
LOWERDB should always be greater than the typical amplitude of those fluctuations deemed insignificant. In
some cases, the width of the dead-band may set to zero (i.e., UPPERDB = LOWERDB). At first glance, this
would seem to make indeterminate the current zone when an integer value sits on the limit. This is not the case,
however, when movement of the value is considered. To illustrate, an example is given, assuming that
UPPERDB = LOWERDB = 100.
Transition from one zone into another generates a collection event, as might be reported via S6, F11. The host
has the option of receiving notification by enabling event reporting for the event. For each variable that has
monitoring capability, one CEID is reserved to indicate zone transitions for that variable.
The sampling frequency is an important aspect of Limits Monitoring. If the value changes frequently compared
to sampling frequency, it is possible for some zone transitions to be missed or for multiple zone transitions to
                                                       48
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


occur between readings. Since it is possible for zone transitions to occur “simultaneously” and for limit
boundaries to be identical, the "event limit" data variable allows a list of multiple zone transitions of a variable
to be reported with a single collection event.
13.1.2     Limits Monitoring State Diagram

                                      LIMIT
                                    MONITORING
                                                          DISABLED



                                                      1              2



                                                          c              ENABLED


                                                              3
                                            BELOW                        ABOVE
                                             LIMIT                        LIMIT
                                                              4


                                                5                         6



                                                          NO ZONE




13.1.3     Limits Monitoring State Definitions Table
13.1.3.1    ABOVE LIMIT
A variable is considered to be above a limit when its value increases to equal or exceed the upper boundary of
the dead-band, UPPERDB. The significance attached to this state is a function of the host's usage.
13.1.3.2    BELOW LIMIT
A variable is considered to be below a limit when its value decreases to equal or fall below the lower boundary
of the dead-band, LOWERDB. The significance attached to this state is a function of the host's usage.
13.1.3.3    NO ZONE
In some circumstances, it is possible for the variable value to be in neither the upper zone nor the lower zone.
This may occur upon definition of a new limit or upon equipment startup when the value of the variable lies in
the dead-band. In this case, the active state of the limit is considered NO ZONE. The limit remains in this state
until the variable value reaches either boundary of the dead-band.

                              defined with S2,                                             determined by the current value of
                              F45.                                                         the monitored variable.
2        ENABLED              Limit attributes set    DISABLED                    None     None
                              to undefined with
                              S2, F45.
3        BELOW LIMIT          Variable increased to   ABOVE LIMIT                 None     Zone Transition
                              be ≥ UPPERDB.
4        ABOVE LIMIT          Variable decreases      BELOW LIMIT                 None     Zone Transition
                              to be ≤ LOWERDB.

                              to be ≤ LOWERDB.

14 Trace Data Collection
14.1 Objective
               To provide the Host system with the means to sample data on a regular basis

14.2 Trace Data Collection
               The Host using S2F23 messages defines trace reports. This will be removed from the SPTS
               fxP equipment when the report has been sent to the Host.
               The value of the required variables is read at the specified time, however, the transmission of
               the S6F1 message may occur sometime later depending upon message traffic.
               Sixteen separate simultaneous Trace operations are allowed, but each must have a unique
               Trace ID (TRID).




                                                    51
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



15 Remote Control
15.1 Objective
                 To provide the Host system with the means to control the SPTS fxP equipment remotely.
                 The Equipment can only be controlled when the Control State is On-line Remote.

15.2 Automatic Equipment Processing Commands
                 The Process State Model of the Machine can be mapped independently onto both cassettes.
                 Therefore two state machines exist, one for VCE A and one for VCE B.
                 The cassette remote commands available to the user are as follows (they are all in upper case):

      RCMD                 CPNAME                        CPVAL         CPVAL
                                                         FORMAT

                                                        56
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


In addition to this state model, the PAUSE and RESUME commands can be used to temporarily suspend and
resume processing. The PAUSE command is available in any state apart from IDLE, SELECTED and
SELECTING if the Process Pause State is ‘Not Paused’. When the PAUSE command is issued, processing
continues until all modules have completed their current action. The Process Pause State then becomes ‘Paused’.
The RESUME command is available when the Process Pause State is ‘Paused’.
Commands available to the Host whilst in the REMOTE Control State are configurable by equipment constants.
If the command is available to the Host, it is made unavailable to the local operator and vice versa.
Also, modules not involved in automatic processing whilst in the REMOTE Control State are available to be
used by a local operator.
Note that, where necessary, remote commands will be interpreted as ‘request action to be initiated’ rather than
‘do action’. The SPTS fxP equipment will then respond via S2, F42 with HCACK = 4 meaning that the
command ‘is going to be performed’.



15.3 Process Module Processing Commands
There is also a Process State Model for each Process Module . Each has its own state machine.
The Process Module remote commands available to the user are as follows (they are all in upper case): -



      RCMD               CPNAME               CPVAL          CPVAL
                                              FORMAT

      “IDLE”             “PM”                 A[1..2]        ‘1’ to ‘6’
                         “RECIPE”             A[20]          Module Recipe Name String
      “READY”            “PM”                 A[1..2]        ‘1’ to ‘6’
                         “RECIPE”             A[20]          Module Recipe Name String
      “PROCESS”          “PM”                 A[1..2]        ‘1’ to ‘6’
                         “RECIPE”             A[20]          Module Recipe Name String
      “SERVICE”          “PM”                 A[1..2]        ‘1’ to ‘6’
                         “RECIPE”             A[20]          Module Recipe Name String
      “ABORTPM”          “PM”                 A[1..2]        ‘1’ to ‘6’
      “HOLD”             “PM”                 A[1..2]        ‘1’ to ‘6’
      “RESTORE”          “PM”                 A[1..2]        ‘1’ to ‘6’

                                 Table 12: Process Module Remote Commands

In order to simplify the model, the transitory states (e.g. ACTION IDLE) are not in the diagram but these are
explained in the State Transition Table.
The initial state entered by the module is different depending on whether the Process Module (PM) runs on a
200 series-based rack or a PC104 PC.
For a 200 series-based PM, the initial state is DOWNLOADING which is entered when the PM code is
downloaded from the CTC to the module.
For a PC104 PM, the initial state is RESET which is entered when the PM code starts running.
The state transition diagram for the Process Module State Diagram is as follows: -

It is also possible for the module to receive the Ready and Process commands from the Aborted, Shutdown and
Idle states, in which case the module goes through the appropriate transitory states.



15.4 Process Module Mode Command

As well as having a state, a Process Module also has a mode. The module is in one of two modes: -

        Automatic – in this mode, the module is available for Automatic Processing of wafers and not available
         for Manual Commands.

        Manual – in this mode, the module is available for Manual Commands and not available for Automatic
         Processing of wafers.


A Remote command is available to allow a Process Module to change mode.
The structure of the command is as follows: -

        RCMD             CPNAME                 CPVAL          CPVAL
                                                FORMAT

        “MODE”           “PM”                   A[1..2]        ‘1’ to ‘6’
                         “MODE”                 A[1..9]        ‘MANUAL’ or ‘AUTOMATIC’




The mode command will be rejected (HCACK = 2) if the Process Module is already in that mode.
An event will be sent when a Process Module changes mode (see collection events table for details).




15.5 Remote-to-Local / Local-to-Remote Command
A Remote command is available to allow the host to switch the control mode, whilst Online-Communicating,
from local to remote or vice-versa.
The structure of the command is as follows: -

        RCMD             CPNAME                 CPVAL          CPVAL
                                                FORMAT

        “LOCAL”          N/A                    N/A            N/A
        “REMOTE”         N/A                    N/A            N/A


An event will be sent when the control state changes (see collection events table for details).




15.6 Acknowledgement Commands
Remote commands are available to allow the host to acknowledge the following :-

   Acknowledge all current alarms – the alarms will then be cleared (including the lamp tower).

   Acknowledge that operator attention is required – this will clear operator attention is required.

                                                          60
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


   Acknowledge alarms and operator attention required.
The structure of the command is as follows: -

      RCMD                     CPNAME           CPVAL         CPVAL
                                                FORMAT

      “ACKFAULTS”              N/A              N/A           N/A
      “ACKOPERATOR”            N/A              N/A           N/A
      “ACKALL”                 N/A              N/A           N/A




15.7 Lamp Tower Commands
Remote commands are available for giving the host control of the operation of the lamp tower. Each individual
lamp and the buzzer can be controlled separately by use of the following message:-

      RCMD                 CPNAME               CPVAL        CPVAL
                                                FORMAT

      “LAMPTOWER”          “LAMPID”             A[1]         Lamp (‘1’, ‘2’, ‘3’ or ’4’) or Alarm (‘5’)
                           “LAMPACTION”         A[1]         ‘1’ = on, ‘2’ = off, ‘3’ - intermittent


Availability of this message for individual lamps is governed by the value of the equipment constants 1000347 –
1000350. See Section 12.6 for further details of these equipment constants.




                                                       61
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



16 Process Program Management
16.1 Objective
To provide a mechanism where the Host and SPTS fxP equipment can transfer process programs and share the
management of them in an orderly manner.



16.2 Description
The SPTS fxP equipment provides a full set of functions for Process Program Management. This allows
Cassette/Wafer Recipes (and the dependent Wafer Recipes, Module Recipes and Conditioning Recipes) to be
transferred as unformatted process program to and from the Host.
There is an Equipment Constant which defines whether Wafer Recipes or Cassette Recipes are
Uploaded/Downloaded. For 200mm tools this EC should be set to Cassette Recipes.


The messages supported are as follows:-

                            Operation                             Unformatted
            Host-initiated Download                         S7F3/S7F4

            Host-initiated Upload                           S7F5/S7F6

            Host-initiated Delete                           S7F17/S7F18

            Host-initiated Directory request                S7F19/S7F20

            Equipment-initiated Upload                      S7F3/S7F4

            Equipment-initiated Download                    S7F5/S7F6




16.2.1   Individual Recipe Upload/Download
Individual recipes can be uploaded or downloaded instead of complete recipe structures. This is controlled by
equipment constant ECID 1000358. The possible values for this, and their meanings, are listed below.
The default value is to disable the use of this new feature and behave as before.
When being used, this feature will affect the functionality of S7F3, S7F5, S7F17, S7F19 to act on the selected
type of recipe only, i.e. no sub-recipe will be included in the operations.

Possible values for ECID 1000358:
0 = Disable the use of individual recipe control
1 = PM1 Module Recipe
2 = PM2 Module Recipe
3 = PM3 Module Recipe
4 = PM4 Module Recipe
5 = PM5 Module Recipe
6 = PM6 Module Recipe
7 = Coolstation Recipe
8 = Conditioning Recipe
9 = Wafer Recipe
10 = Cassette Recipe

In addition to this, ECID 1000359 can be used to specify whether process or service type recipes for a module
are used.
0 = Process Recipe
1 = Service Recipe

                                                       62
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


16.2.2    Custom message (S7F65/66) for Reporting Child Recipes
A custom message is supported to allow child recipes of cassette, wafer or conditioning recipes to be requested
by the host.
The type of recipe is controlled by the settings of ECIDs 1000358, 1000359 and 1000194.
The format of the messages are as follows:-
S7 F65
 < A RecipeName>

Success
S7 F66
L,2
          1.   <Bo True>
          2.   L,n
                   1. L,2
                             1. <A RecipeType>
                             2. <A RecipeName>

The RecipeType string will be WaferRecipe, ConditioningRecipe or the name of the module if a module recipe.

Failure
L,2
          1.   <Bo False>
          2.   L,n
                   1. L,2
                             1. <U4 ErrorCode>
                             2. <A ErrorText>




16.3 Restrictions
Only unformatted process programs are supported, there is no support for formatted process programs.

Recipes downloaded from the Host will automatically overwrite recipes held locally on the Equipment.

Host-initiated delete will only delete the relevant Wafer or Cassette Recipe and will not delete the various sub-
recipes.




                                                        63
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx




17 Terminal Services

17.1 Objective
Terminal Services allows simple text communication between the Host and Equipment Operator.

17.2 Description
Terminal Services allows text strings to be sent between the Host and Equipment. There is an indicator on the
CTC to allow the operator to see that a new Terminal message has arrived and has not been recognized.
Terminal Services are implemented as specified in the GEM standard :-


       Any new Terminal message sent be the Host overwrites an ‘unrecognised’ message at the CTC.

       The SPTS fxP equipment allows a message of up to 160 characters to be sent or received.

       The SPTS fxP equipment provides an easy mechanism for reading a message sent by the Host.

       The SPTS fxP equipment provides an indicator to notify an operator when an unrecognized message is
        present

       The SPTS fxP equipment provides an easy mechanism for message recognition.

       The SPTS fxP equipment provides a method for entering an alpha-numeric text message.

       The SPTS fxP equipment interprets a Host message with zero-length TEXT data item as replacing any
        previous unrecognized message but does not consider it as an unrecognized message. This provides a
        method of clearing an unrecognized message and turning off the unrecognized indicator.


The messages supported are as follows:-

                            Operation
            Host-initiated Terminal Message                S10F3/S10F4

            Equipment-initiated Terminal Message           S10F1/S10F2




The SPTS fxP equipment provides a collection event when a message is recognized by the operator.




                                                      64
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



18 Clock
18.1 Objective
               To provide an orderly synchronization of Equipment to Host Date and Time.


18.2 Description
               The SPTS fxP equipment fully supports the Clock capability including the use of the
               equipment constant TIMEFORMAT in order to be Year 2000 compliant.
               The following features are supported: -

                  Host-initiated Date/Time Set (S2F31/S2F32)

                  Host-initiated Date/Time Request (S2F17/S2F18)

                  Equipment-initiated Date/Time Request (S2F17/S2F18)


               When the SPTS fxP equipment receives a new Date/Time from the Host via an S2F31 or
               S2F18, it modifies the equipment’s clock hardware.




                                                    65
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



19 Appendix A - Message Summary Tables
19.1 Control State Dependency
The equipment's Control State Model determines the availability of most SECS-II message communication. If
the host sends an unavailable SECS-II message while the equipment is off-line, then the equipment will respond
with a respective Sx, F0 message.
Control State         Description
On-line L, R          On-line local or remote
Any                   Any control state
Off-line              Off-line equipment, host or on-line Attempt. It may be accepted while on-line, but has no
                      meaning.
On-line R             On-line remote

20 Appendix B - Streams and Functions
The sections below describe the subset of SECS-II message streams and their included functions that are
supported by the interface. It can be seen that the odd numbered functions within each stream are requests and
the subsequent, even numbered functions are the corresponding response.
Symbol              Description
HE                 Host to equipment or equipment to host
HE                 Equipment to host only
HE                 Host to equipment only

20.1 Stream 1: Equipment Status
20.1.1   S1, F1 Are You There Request (HE)
Establishes that the SECS-II link is operational and that the host and machine are on-line. The machine responds
with its model number and software revision. The host responds with a null list. The machine periodically sends
this message as a ``heartbeat’’ for the SECS-II communications link.
Header only
20.1.2 S1, F2 On-line Data (HE)
L, 2
1. <A MDLN>
       2. <A SOFTREV>
20.1.3   S1, F2 On-line Data (HE)
L, 0
20.1.4   S1, F3 Selected Equipment Status Request (HE)
A request from the host system to the machine, to identify the value of certain status variables in a predefined
order.
L, n
         1. <U4 SVID>
         …
         n. <U4 SVID>
A zero-length list or item means report all SVID.
20.1.5   S1, F4 Selected Equipment Status Data (HE)
L, n
       1. <* SV>
       n. <* SV>
n. A, Bi, Bo, F4, F8, L, I1, I2, I4, U1, U2, U4
A zero-length U1 for SV means that the SVID does not exist.
20.1.6   S1, F11 Status Variable Namelist Request (HE)
A request from the host to the machine to report the name and units of certain status variables, in the order
requested.
L, n
         1. <U4 SVID>
         …
         n. <U4 SVID>
A zero-length means report all SVID.
20.1.7   S1, F12 Status Variable Namelist Reply (HE)
L, n
         1. L, 3
               1. <U4 SVID>
               2. <A SVNAME>
               3. <A UNITS>
         …
         n. L, 3
                                                        74
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


                   1. <U4 SVID>
                   2. <A SVNAME>
                   3. <A UNITS>
20.1.8   S1, F13 Establish Communications Request (HE)
Initiate an attempt to establish a SECS-II communications link at a logical level on power-up or after a break in
the link. It is the first message sent after either of the above conditions.
L, 0
20.1.9   S1, F14 Establish Communications Request Acknowledge (HE)
L, 2
         1. <Bi COMMACK>
         2. L, 0
20.1.10 S1, F13 Establish Communications Request (HE)
Initiate an attempt to establish a SECS-II communications link at a logical level on power-up or after a break in
the link. It is the first message sent after either of the above conditions. If no response is received from the host,
the machine will periodically send a S1F13 message until a S1F14 with the correct COMMACK is received.
L, 2
         1. <A MDLN>
         2. <A SOFTREV>
20.1.11 S1, F14 Establish Communications Request Acknowledge (HE)
L, 2
        1. <Bi COMMACK>
        2. L, 2
                1. <A MDLN>
                2. <A SOFTREV>
20.1.12 S1, F15 Off-line Control State Request (HE)
A request from the host that the machine change control state to off-line.
Header only
20.1.13 S1, F16 Off-line Control State Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi OFLACK>
20.1.14 S1, F17 On-line Control State Request (HE)
A request from the host that the machine enters the On-line State in its control model.
Header only
20.1.15 S1, F18 On-line Control State Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi ONLACK>

20.2 Stream 2: Equipment Control and Diagnostics
20.2.1   S2, F13 Equipment Constant Request (HE)
A request from the host to report the value of certain equipment constants in a predefined order.
L, n
         1. <U4 ECID>
         …
         n. <U4 ECID>
A zero-length list or item means report all ECID.
20.2.2   S2, F14 Equipment Constant Data (HE)
L, n
       1. <* ECV>
       …
       n. <* ECV>
n. A, Bi, Bo, F4, F8, I1, I2, I4, U1, U2, U4
A zero-length U1 ECV means that ECID does not exist.
                                                   75
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


20.2.3   S2, F15 New Equipment Constant Send (HE)
Host updates the values of specified EC. If the host returns a non-zero EAC the machine cannot alter the value
of any ECID specified in the S2F15 body.
L, n
       1. L, 2
                <U4 ECID>
                <* ECV>
       …
       n. L, 2
                <U4 ECID>
                <* ECV>
n. A, Bi, Bo, F4, F8, I1, I2, I4, U1, U2, U4
20.2.4 S2, F16 New Equipment Constant Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi EAC>
20.2.5   S2, F17 Date and Time Request (HE)
The host and machine synchronize time-stamps.
Header Only
20.2.6   S2, F18 Date and Time Data (HE)
<A TIME>
A zero-length item means no time exists.
20.2.7   S2, F23 Trace Initialize Send (HE)
The host requests a time driven trace of specified status variables. If TOTSMP is zero, the machine will cancel
an existing trace with the given TRID.
L, 5
         1. <U4 TRID>
         2. <A DSPER>
         3. <U4 TOTSMP>
         4. <U4 REPGSZ>
         5. L, n
                   1. <U4 SVID>
                   …
                   n. <U4 SVID>
20.2.8 S2, F24 Trace Initialize Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi TIAACK>
20.2.9   S2, F25 Loop-back Diagnostic Request (HE)
The host sends an arbitrary binary string to test the operation of the logical link.
<* ABS>
n. Any structure is valid.
20.2.10 S2, F26 Loop-back Diagnostic Data (HE)
<* ABS>
n. The same structure is returned.
20.2.11 S2, F29 Equipment Constant Namelist Request (HE)
A request from the host to the machine to identify certain equipment constants. A null list (n = 0) is interpreted
as send information on all ECID.
L, n
         1. <U4 ECID>
         …
         n. <U4 ECID>
A zero-length list means send all information for all ECID.



                                                          76
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


20.2.12 S2, F30 Equipment Constant Namelist (HE)
L, n
        1. L, 6
                1. <U4 ECID>
                2. <A ECNAME>
                3. <* ECMIN>
                3. <* ECMAX>
                3. <* ECDEF>
                3. <A UNITS>
        …
        n. L, 6
                1. <U4 ECID>
                2. <A ECNAME>
                3. <* ECMIN>
                3. <* ECMAX>
                3. <* ECDEF>
                3. <A UNITS>
n. A, Bi, Bo, F4, F8, L, I1, I2, I4, U1, U2, U4
20.2.13 S2, F31 Date and Time Set Request (HE)
The host instructs the equipment to set its time base to the specified value.
<A TIME>
20.2.14 S2, F32 Date and Time Set Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi TIACK>
20.2.15 S2, F33 Define Report (HE)
A request from the host for the machine to define a group of event reports. One or more Report IDs is specified,
each containing a list of variable IDs to be included in the report.
L, 2
         1. <U4 DATAID>
         2. L, a
                   1. L, 2
                           1. <U4 RPTID>
                           2. L, b
                                  1. <U4 VID>
                                  …
                                  b. <U4 VID>
                   …
                   a. L, 2
                           1. <U4 RPTID>
                           2. L, c
                                  1. <U4 VID>
                                  …
                                  c. <U4 VID>
A zero-length list following DATAID deletes all report definitions and associated links. See S2, F35.
A zero-length list following RPTID deletes report type RPTID. All CEID links to this RPTID are also deleted.
20.2.16 S2, F34 Define Report Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi DRACK>
20.2.17 S2, F35 Link Event Report (HE)
The host links Report IDs (RPTID) to Collection event IDs (CEID). These linked event reports default to
"disabled" upon linking. That is, the occurrence of an event would not cause the report to be sent until enabled.
See S2, F37 for enabling events.
L, 2
         1. <U4 DATAID>
         2. L, a
               1. L, 2
                     1. <U4 CEID>
                                                         77
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


                           2. L, b
                                 1. <RPTID>
                                 …
                                 b. <RPTID>
                   …
                   a. L, 2
                           1. <CEID>
                           2. L, c
                                   1. <RPTID>
                                   …
                                   c. <RPTID>
A zero-length list following CEID deletes all report links to that event.
20.2.18 S2, F36 Link Event Report Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi LRACK>
20.2.19 S2, F37 Enable/Disable Event Report (HE)
Host requests to enable or disable reporting for a list of Collection events (CEID).
L, 2
         1. <Bo CEED>
         2. L, n
                   1. <U4 CEID>
                   …
                   n. <U4 CEID>
A zero-length list means all CEID.
20.2.20 S2, F38 Enable/Disable Event Report Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi ERACK>
20.2.21 S2, F39 Multi-Block Inquire (HE)
The host initiates this transaction preceding a multi-block S2, F33 or S2, F35.
L, 2
         1. <DATAID>
         2. <DATALENGTH>
20.2.22 S2, F40 Multi-Block Grant (HE)
<Bi GRANT>
20.2.23 S2, F41 Host Command Send (HE)
The host sends a command to the machine for execution with the relevant parameters.
L, 2
         1. <A RCMD>
         2. L, n
               1. L, 2
                     1. <A CPNAME>
                     2. <A CPVAL>
               …
               n. L, 2
                     1. <A CPNAME>
                     2. <A CPVAL>
20.2.24 S2, F42 Host Command Acknowledge (HE)
L, 2
        1. <HCACK>
        2. L, n
                1. L, 2
                       1. <A CPNAME>
                       2. <Bi CPACK>
                …
                n. L, 2
                       1. <Bi CPNAME>
                       2. <A CPACK>
                                            78
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


If there are no invalid parameters, then a list of zero length will be sent for item 2.
20.2.25 S2, F43 Reset Spooling Streams and Functions (HE)
The host selects specific streams and functions to be spooled whenever spooling is active.
L, m
        1. L, 2
                 1. <U1 STRID>
                 2. L, n
                           1. <U1 FCNID>
                           …
                           n. <U1 FCNID>
        …
        m. L, 2
                 1. <U1 STRID>
                 2. L, n
                           1. <U1 FCNID>
                           …
                           n. <U1 FCNID>
   A zero-length list, m = 0, turns off spooling for all streams and functions.
   A zero-length list, n = 0, turns on spooling for all functions for the associated stream
   Turning off spooling for all functions for a specific stream is achieved by omitting reference to the stream
    from this message.
   Spooling for Stream 1 is not allowed.
   All other primary messages for a stream are allowed.
   A defined list of functions for a stream in this message will replace any previously selected functions.
20.2.26 S2, F44 Reset Spooling Acknowledge (HE)
L, 2
         1. <Bi RSACK>
         2. L, m
                   1. L, 3
                             1. <U1 STRID>
                             2. <Bi STRACK>
                             3. L, n
                                      1. <U1 FCNID>
                                      …
                                      n. <U1 FCNID>
                   …
                   m. L, 3
                             1. <U1 STRID>
                             2. <Bi STRACK>
                             3. L, n
                                      1. <U1 FCNID>
                                      …
                                      n. <U1 FCNID>
If RSACK = 0, then a zero-length list, m = 0, is given. This indicates no streams or functions are in error.
A zero-length list, n = 0, indicates no functions in error for specified streams.

        1. <U4 DATAID>
        2. L, m
                1. L, 2
                        1. <U4 VID>
                        2. L, n

                                                 1. <* UPPERDB>

                                                          79
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


                                     …
                                     n. L, 2
                                           1. <Bi LIMITID>
                                           2. L, p = {0,2}
                                                 1. <* UPPERDB>
                                                 2. <* LOWERDB>
                …
                m. L, 2
                1. L, 2
                           1. <U4 VID>
                           2. L, n

                                                   2. <* LOWERDB>
n. A, Bi, Bo, F4, F8, I1, I2, I4, U1, U2, U4
A zero length list, m=0, sets all limit values for all monitored VID to "undefined".
A zero length list, n=0, sets all limit values for that VID to "undefined".
A zero length list, p=0, sets that limit to "undefined".
20.2.28 S2, F46 Variable Limit Attribute Acknowledge (HE)
Acknowledge definition of variable limit attributes or report error. If DVLA is not accepted due to one or more
invalid parameters (e.g., LIMITACK=3), then a list of invalid parameters is returned containing the variable
limit attribute and reason for rejection. If an error condition is detected, the entire message is rejected, i.e.,
partial changes are not allowed.
L, 2
         1. <Bi VLACK>
         2. L, m
                   1. L, 3
                             1. <U4 VID>
                             2. <Bi LVACK>
                             3. L, n = {0,2}
                                      1. <Bi LIMITID>
                                      2. <Bi LIMITACK>
                   …
                   m. L, 3
                             1. <U4 VID>
                             2. <Bi LVACK>
                             3. L, n = {0,2}
                                      1. <Bi LIMITID>
                                      2. <Bi LIMITACK>
A zero-length list, m = 0, indicates no invalid variable limit attributes.
A zero-length list, n = 0, indicates no invalid limit values for that VID.
20.2.29 S2, F47 Variable Limit Attribute Request (HE)
Host requests the current variable limit attribute definitions. This message allows the host to query the
equipment for the current limit-attribute definitions.
L, m
         1. <U4 VID>
         …
         m. <U4 VID>
A zero-length list, m = 0, requests a list of all VID values that can have variable limit attributes.

SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


20.2.30 S2, F48 Variable Limit Attribute Send (HE)
L, m
        1. L, 2
                1. <U4 VID>
                2. L, p = {0,4}
                           1. <A UNITS>
                           2. <* LIMITMIN>
                           3. <* LIMITMAX>
                           4. L, n
                                    1. L, 3
                                             1. <Bi LIMITID>

                                             3. <* LOWERDB>

                                    n. L, 3

        m. L, 2

                           1. <A UNITS>
