                           3. <* LIMITMAX>
                           4. L, n
                                    1. L, 3
                                             1. <Bi LIMITID>
                                             2. <* UPPERDB>
                                             3. <* LOWERDB>
                                    …
                                    n. L, 3
                                             1. <Bi LIMITID>
                                             2. <* UPPERDB>
                                             3. <* LOWERDB>
n. A, Bi, Bo, F4, F8, I1, I2, I4, U1, U2, U4
A zero-length list, p = 0, indicates that limits are not supported for the VID.
A zero-length list, n = 0, means no limits are currently defined for the specified variable.




20.3 Stream 5: Exception Reporting
20.3.1   S5, F1 Alarm Report Send (HE)
This message reports a change in a defined alarm. Thus, both setting and clearing an alarm will have distinct
alarms.
L, 3
         1. <Bi ALCD>
         2. <U4 ALID>
         3. <A ALTX>
20.3.2 S5, F2 Alarm Report Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi ACKC5>
20.3.3   S5, F3 Enable/Disable Alarm Send (HE)
This message enables or disables an alarm from being reported to the host. Some alarms (safety related) are not
controllable in this way.
L, 2
         1. <Bi ALED>
                                                         81
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


         2. <U4 ALID>
A zero-length item for ALID means all alarms.
20.3.4 S5, F4 Enable/Disable Alarm Acknowledge (HE)
<Bi ACKC5>
20.3.5   S5, F5 List Alarms Request (HE)
The host requests the machine to send information on currently defined alarms.
L, n
         1. <U4 ALID>
         …
         n. <U4 ALID>
A zero-length item means send all possible alarms regardless of the state of ALED.
20.3.6   S5, F6 List Alarms Data (HE)
L, m
         1. L, 3
                  1. <Bi ALCD>
                  2. <U4 ALID>
                  3. <A ALTX>
         …
         m. L, 3
                  1. <Bi ALCD>
                  2. <U4 ALID>
                  3. <A ALTX>
If m = 0, no response can be made. A zero-length item returned for ALCD or ALTX means that value does not
    exist.

20.4.1   S6, F1 Trace Data Send (HE)

20.4.2   S6, F2 Trace Data Acknowledge (HE)

20.6 Stream 9: System Errors
20.6.1   S9, F1 Unrecognized Device ID (HE)
Device ID specified in block header is not defined in the machine.
<Bi MHEAD>
20.6.2   S9, F3 Unrecognized Stream Type (HE)
Machine does not recognize the stream type in the message block header.
<Bi MHEAD>
20.6.3   S9, F5 Unrecognized Function Type (HE)
Machine does not recognize the function type in the message block header.
<Bi MHEAD>
20.6.4   S9, F7 Illegal Data (HE)
This error signifies that the stream and function were correctly interpreted but the associated data was not.
<Bi MHEAD>



                                                        85
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


20.6.5   S9, F9 Transaction Timer Timeout (HE)
This error specifies that a transaction / receive timer has timed out and the transaction aborted. The host system
should respond to this message in a suitable manner to keep the system operational.
<Bi SHEAD>
20.6.6   S9, F11 Data Too Long (HE)
The machine has been sent more data than it can handle.
<Bi MHEAD>
20.6.7   S9, F13 Conversation Timeout (HE)
Machine informs host that data was expected, but none was received within time period given.
L, 2
         1. <A MEXP>
         2. <A EDID>

22 Appendix D - Module Equipment Specific
   Equipment Constants
NB: The equipment constants in this section are not intended to be modified by the host.
Due to the fact that most module types can be configured for most positions on the SPTS fxP Equipment, the
following rules are used to work out the Equipment Constant identifiers (ECID) for the modules.
The ECID is computed from the following equation:
EC ID = (station number * 100000) + (station type offset * 1000) + 1001000 + config Id offset;
(1001000 is added to make sure that the computed ECID clears any other VID defined.)


Station Number :-         0 = Transport
                          1 = VCE A
                          2 = Process Module 1
                          3 = Process Module 2
                          4 = Process Module 3
                          5 = Process Module 4
                          6 = Process Module 5
                          7 = Process Module 6
                          8 = VCE B
                          10 = Cool Station


Station Type :-           4 = Sputter Deposition PM
                          7 = HSE PM
                          9 = Heat PM
                          20 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks MX Transport
                          21 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks Coolstation
                          22 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks MX Cassette
                          23 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks Inliner
                          24 = Etch PM
                          25 = Deposition RevB PM
                          26 = SoftEtch RevB PM
                          27 = Heat RevB PM
                          46 = C3M (Bridge)
                          53=Primaxx Monarch 25
                          56 = c2L Transport
                          58 = Pro CVE PM

The module equipment constants together with their config id offsets are defined as follows
(the complete name of each variable is StatX Y Z EquipmentConstantName where X is the station number Y is
the station type and Z is the Config section name)

       SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx

23 Appendix E - Module Equipment Specific Status
   Variables
Due to the fact that most module types can be configured for most positions on the SPTS fxP Equipment, the
following rules are used to work out the variable identifiers (VID) for the modules.
The VID is computed from the following equation:
VID = (station number * 10000) + (station type offset* 100) + (variable offset) + 10000
(10000 is added to make sure that the computed VID clears any other VID defined for general use.)
Station Number :-         0 = Transport
                          1 = VCE A
                          2 = Process Module 1
                          3 = Process Module 2
                          4 = Process Module 3
                          5 = Process Module 4
                          6 = Process Module 5
                          7 = Process Module 6
                          8 = VCE B
                          10 = Cool Station
Station Type :-            3 = Forcefill PM
                           4 = Sputter Deposition PM
                           7 = HSE PM
                           9 = Heat PM
                           20 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks MX Transport
                           21 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks Coolstation
                           22 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks MX Cassette
                           24 = Etch PM
                           25 = Deposition RevB PM
                           26 = SoftEtch RevB PM
                           27 = Heat RevB PM
                           46 = C3M (Bridge)
                           53 = Primaxx Monarch 25
                           56 = c2L Transport
                           58 = Pro CVE PM




 (the complete name of each variable is StatX Y MV VariableName or StatX Y DSV VariableName where X is
the station number and Y is the station type, MV is used for analogue values and DSV is used for digital values).

        SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx

24 Appendix F – Status Variable Value Definitions
24.1 Station Type
0 = Station Not Fitted
5 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks MX Transport
12 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks MX Cassette
22 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks Coolstation
31 = GTM/Level 1 Brooks Inliner
40 = Sputter Deposition PM
41 = Deposition RevB PM
55 = HSE PM
57 = SoftEtch RevB PM
86 = C3M (Bridge)
90 = Heat PM
91 = Heat RevB PM
100 = Buffer Station
123 = Pro CVE PM
169 = Delta APM PM
180 = Etch MORI PM
181 = Etch PERIE PM
182 = Etch ICP PM
183 = Etch ISOPOD PM
184 = Etch GPE PM
185 = Etch DSI PM
221 = Primaxx Monarch 25
222 = c2L Transport
255 = Invalid Station
999 = Dummy Station

24.2 Robot Position
0 = Unknown
1 = Home
11 = Arm A at VCE A
12 = Arm A at PM1
13 = Arm A at PM2
14 = Arm A at PM3
15 = Arm A at PM4
16 = Arm A at PM5
17 = Arm A at PM6
18 = Arm A at VCE B
19 = Arm A at Aligner
20 = Arm A At TopCooler
31 = Arm B at VCE A
32 = Arm B at PM1
33 = Arm B at PM2
34 = Arm B at PM3
35 = Arm B at PM4
36 = Arm B at PM5
37 = Arm B at PM6
38 = Arm B at VCE B
39 = Arm B at Aligner
40 = Arm B At TopCooler
50 = Error




                                               213
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


24.3 Robot Station Number
1 = VCEA
2 = PM1
3 = PM2
4 = PM3
5 = PM4
6 = PM5
7 = PM6
8 = VCEB
9 = Aligner
10 = TopCooler
11 = Buffer
255 = Unknown

24.4 Wafer Status
PMs and VCEs report Wafer Status as arrays.
For VCEs, each element in the array represents a slot in the cassette.
For PMs, only the first element of the array is valid since all PMs have only a single wafer slot.

1 = No Wafer

24.5 Station States
0 = Undefined
1 = Reset
2 = Config
3 = Shutdown (Ejected for Brooks Cassette)
4 = Idle (Loaded for Brooks Cassette)
5 = Process
6 = Busy
7 = Service
8 = Held
9 = Aborted
10 = Ready
11 = Going to Shutdown (Ejecting for Brooks Cassette)
12 = Going to Idle (Loading for Brooks Cassette)
13 = Processing
14 = Servicing
15 = Going to Hold
16 = Going to Abort
17 = Going to Ready
18 = Download
19 = Disconnected
20 = Unknown
25 = Handling
30= Mapping
31 = Closing
32 = Closed



                                                   220
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


24.6 Wafer Tracking Status Variable
The wafer tracking status variable is a string that contains each station location that a wafer has visited during its
time at the machine. There is a separate variable for each wafer of each cassette. The first entry for a wafer will
always be the cassette station once the cassette is loaded at that station. The variable is cleared whenever a
cassette is removed from the VCE.
The characters in the string represent stations as follows:-
a = Arm A
b = Arm B
1 = VCE A
2 = PM 1
3 = PM 2
4 = PM 3
5 = PM 4
6 = PM 5
7 = PM 6
8 = VCE B
9 = Aligner
A = Cooler
B = Buffer
For example, the status variable VCEAWaferTrackingW01 would contain the string “1a9a2a1” for a wafer that
was moved from VCE A to Arm A, aligned and then transferred to PM1 then transferred back to VCE A using
Arm A again.




                                                         221
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


24.7 Energy Consumption Data
The equipment monitors the consumption of raw materials and stores the data in a local database. The data is
accessible as daily, weekly, monthly and yearly values and as a grand total.
Data stored is:
Sputter Deposition Process Module:

Material          Units                                           DataName

Gases             BL                                              PMx Gas Count

RF Power          KW.Hours                                        PMx Acc Power



HSE Process Module:

Material          Units                                           DataName

Gases             BL                                              PMx Gas Count

Coil Power        KW.Hours                                        PMx Coil Power



Where x denotes the Process Module number 0 - 5
Data is returned in the format:
L, n
         1. L, 6
               1. <A DataName1>
               2. L, 3
                     1. A, "DayTotal"
                     2. <F8, Day Total>
                     3. <A, Units>
               3. L, 3
                     1. A, "WeekTotal"
                     2. <F8, Week Total>
                     3. <A, Units>
               4. L, 3
                     1. A, "MonthTotal"
                     2. <F8, Month Total>
                     3. <A, Units>
               5. L, 3
                     1. A, "YearTotal"
                     2. <F8, Year Total>
                     3. <A, Units>
               6. L, 3
                     4. A, "GrandTotal"
                     5. <F8, Grand Total>
                     6. <A, Units>
               …
         n. L, 6
               1. <A, Datanamen>
               …




                                                      222
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx



25 Appendix G – Wafer Statistical Data
25.1 Statistical Data Collected from Datalogging Database
At the end of each process step an event can now be enabled that has data variables associated with it to provide
the summary information from that last step. This data is retrieved from the datalogging database and provided
in a single DVID as list with similar format to that displayed by the dataviewer (see below for more details on
the format of this variable).

To enable this feature, ECID 5037 (NotifyWaferStatisticalData) must be set to true.

CEID 810 (WaferStatisticalDataAvailable) will then be triggered at the end of each process module recipe step
once the data has been retrieved from the database.
The following DVIDs are valid for this event:-

5100 - WaferStatisticalDataDV
5101 - WaferRecipeDV
5102 - ModuleRecipeDV
5110 - CassetteID
5111 - WaferID
5113 - StationID
5116 – StepID
6102 – PortID

The format of DVID 5100 (WaferStatisticalDataDV) is as described below:-

L, n
         1. L, 5
                   1. <A MV1 Name >
                   2. <A MV1 Units>
                   3. <F4 MV1 Min Value>
                   4. <F4 MV1 Max Value>
                   5. <F4 MV1 Avg Value>
         …
         n. L, 5
                   1. <A MVn Name>
                   2. <A MVn Units>
                   3. <F4 MVn Min Value>
                   4. <F4 MVn Max Value>
                   5. <F4 MVn Avg Value>




                                                       223
SPTS fxP 200mm SECSII Manual (Cimetrix).docx


25.2 Statistical Data as Separate DVIDs
As a new feature in this release, the statistical data is now available as separate DVIDs for min, max and
average for each of the module status variables. These IDs are listed in the following sections for each available
module type (each DVID has the F4 format).
To enable creation of these statistical data DVIDs then ECID 5039 (GenerateStatisticalDVIDs) must be set to
true.
To enable creation of Median and Standard Deviation statistics then ECID 5040
(MedianAndStdDeviationRequired) must be set to true. If this value is set to false then the DVIDs relating to
these statistical values will not be created.
When using this method of obtaining the statistical data it is recommended that ECID 5037
(NotifyWaferStatisticalData) be set to false so that the same data isn’t also being retrieved from the datalogging
database as this will be an unnecessary overhead.
The DVIDs will be valid only at the end of a wafer process step in the process modules in the following
sections. These DVIDs can be linked to the following collection events:

 482                    PM1RecipeStepEnd                      PM1 Recipe step ended
 483                    PM2RecipeStepEnd                      PM2 Recipe step ended
 484                    PM3RecipeStepEnd                      PM3 Recipe step ended
 485                    PM4RecipeStepEnd                      PM4 Recipe step ended
 486                    PM5RecipeStepEnd                      PM5 Recipe step ended
 487                    PM6RecipeStepEnd                      PM6 Recipe step ended
 858                    RecipeStepEnd                         A new recipe step has finished in a process module

25.3 Etch PM Generated Summary Data
A new has been added for higher resolution statistical data being made available over SECSII for Etch modules.
Additionally, the data for looped processes is summarised across multiple loops for each step. This means that
the statistical data presented at the end of the process is for each step as defined in the recipe rather than every
step within every loop, so there is a maximum of 20 summarised steps rather than potentially thousands of
summarised steps.

A new Collection Event (CEID 811) has been introduced which is used to capture this step data. This event will
occur once for each step of the process and will not occur as soon as the process has completed fully – i.e. the
data is not available at the end of each step but only at the end of process.

The following table lists the available DVIDs for the Etch module statistical data items that can be attached to
CEID 811. Additionally, the DVIDs normally associated with the end of a process step can also be used
5101 - WaferRecipeDV
5102 - ModuleRecipeDV
5110 - CassetteID
5111 - WaferID
5113 - StationID
5116 – StepID
6102 – PortID

Etch Process Module Statistical Data Variables:-

        DVID           Name
      12400000         Etch_DV_pressure_Min
      12400001         Etch_DV_pressure_Max
      12400002         Etch_DV_pressure_Avg
      12400004         Etch_DV_pressure_StdDeviation

      12400011         Etch_DV_platenHFPower_Max
      12400012         Etch_DV_platenHFPower_Avg

      12400032         Etch_DV_heBPPressure_Avg
      12400034         Etch_DV_heBPPressure_StdDeviation
      12400040         Etch_DV_gasFlow1_Min
